title: Study permit: Who can apply
text: To come to Canada to study, an applicant must be enrolled at a designated learning institution (DLI). The applicant must also show enough money to pay tuition, living expenses for themselves and any accompanying family members, and return transportation for everyone. The applicant must obey the law, have no criminal record and obtain a police certificate if one is required. The applicant must be in good health and complete a medical exam if required. Finally, the applicant must convince an officer that they will leave Canada when the study permit expires.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: A provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) comes from the province or territory where the student plans to study and confirms that a place is available. It is provided through the designated learning institution and is usually required to apply for a study permit. It must be submitted together with the study permit application, not afterwards, and for each applicant even when a family applies together.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: No PAL or TAL is needed for several groups, including students applying to preschool, primary or secondary school, and students entering a degree-granting master's or doctoral program at a public DLI starting January 1, 2026. Exchange students who pay no tuition to the Canadian institution, and holders of a Global Affairs Canada scholarship, are also exempt. An applicant who claims an exemption must provide proof of it with the application.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
section: How long a PAL/TAL is valid
text: A PAL/TAL is linked to the school the student applies to and normally has to be used in the year it was issued. For the 2026 cap year, a PAL/TAL issued between January 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026 is valid until December 31, 2026. A letter from a previous cap year cannot be used, and an expired letter must be replaced by a new one before applying. A new letter is also needed after a refusal or approval, or when changing schools.

title: Study permit: Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter
text: Students who want to study in Quebec need an attestation of issuance of a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) from the Government of Quebec instead of a PAL. Most students who are exempt from the PAL must still obtain a CAQ. The CAQ must contain the line stating that the applicant has a place in Quebec's share of study permit applications or is exempt from it.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: Applicants must prove they have enough money, without working in Canada, to cover tuition, living expenses for themselves and accompanying family members, and transportation to and from Canada. Funds for the first year of studies must be shown. For programs longer than one year, the applicant must also explain how the whole program will be paid, for example with a multi-year scholarship or employed parents.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: Examples of documents that can show funds include a receipt for the first year of tuition and housing, a student loan from a bank, a scholarship, pay stubs, a signed letter from a sponsor with proof of their occupation and relationship, a Canadian bank account in the applicant's name, a guaranteed investment certificate from a Canadian financial institution, and bank statements for the past six months. The list is not complete and applicants need not provide all of these documents. Bank statements must show where the income comes from.

title: Study permit: Proof of financial support
text: For applications submitted on or after September 1, 2026, outside Quebec, the living expense amount for one person is 23,448 Canadian dollars per year, 29,192 for two people, 35,888 for three, and 43,572 for four. These amounts exclude tuition and transportation costs. For applications between January 1, 2025 and August 31, 2026, the amount for one person was 22,895 dollars. Quebec applicants must follow the costs set by the Quebec immigration ministry.

title: Study permit: How to apply
text: When applying, the applicant should submit the letter of acceptance from the designated learning institution, the provincial or territorial attestation letter, and as many of the other required documents as possible. A study permit cannot be finalized until the application is complete, and waiting to submit documents delays processing. Applications for a study permit must be made online, with limited exceptions such as a disability that prevents online application.

title: Study permit: How to apply
text: Most applicants between 14 and 79 years old must give fingerprints and a photo, called biometrics. The biometrics fee of 85 Canadian dollars for an individual, or at most 170 for families applying together, should be paid when the application is submitted. The applicant has 30 days from the date of the letter to give biometrics, and they are only needed once every 10 years.

title: Student Visa (U.S. Department of State)
text: A student who will attend a university, college, high school, seminary, conservatory, or an academic or language program needs an F visa. Vocational and other recognized non-academic programs, other than language training, require an M visa. The Visa Waiver Program and the B visitor visa cannot be used to study, apart from short recreational courses that give no credit.

title: Student Visa (U.S. Department of State)
text: The applicant must first be accepted by a school approved by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP). The applicant is registered in SEVIS and pays the SEVIS I-901 fee. The school then issues a Form I-20, which the applicant must bring to the visa interview. A spouse and children who will live with the student need their own SEVIS registration and I-20, but they do not pay the SEVIS fee.

title: Student Visa (U.S. Department of State)
text: The student applies at a U.S. embassy or consulate, preferably in the country of residence, and should book early because waiting times vary. An interview is generally required for applicants aged 14 to 79, while those aged 13 or younger or 80 or older usually do not need one. A new student can receive the visa up to 365 days before the program start date but can enter the United States no more than 30 days early. Fingerprints are usually taken at the interview, and administrative processing may follow.

title: Student Visa (U.S. Department of State)
text: The applicant should bring the Form I-20 and evidence of the ability to pay for studies, and should check the embassy or consulate website for the full document list. A visa does not guarantee entry: a Customs and Border Protection officer decides at the port of entry. F-1 students generally must leave within 60 days after the program end date shown on the I-20.

title: Foreign Students in Public Schools (U.S. Department of State)
text: F-1 students can attend public high school, grades 9 through 12, for a maximum of 12 months. An F-1 visa cannot be issued for public elementary school or for publicly funded adult education. The student must pay the school the full unsubsidized per capita cost of the education, which normally ranges from about 3,000 to 10,000 US dollars, and the school cannot waive it. The amount should appear on the Form I-20.

title: I-901 SEVIS Fee Frequently Asked Questions (ICE)
text: Most F-1, F-3, M-1 and M-3 students pay the I-901 SEVIS fee when they first become students. Spouses and children (F-2, M-2, J-2) do not pay. Continuing students who keep their status under the same SEVIS ID generally do not pay again. A school or sponsor may pay on the student's behalf but is not required to, and anyone can pay for the student.

title: I-901 SEVIS Fee Frequently Asked Questions (ICE)
text: The I-901 SEVIS fee is 350 US dollars for students in F-1, F-3, M-1 and M-3 status and 220 US dollars for J-1 exchange visitors. Some short exchange programs such as summer work and travel, au pair or camp counselor cost 35 US dollars. There is no fee for spouses and children, and fee waivers are not available.

title: I-901 SEVIS Fee Frequently Asked Questions (ICE)
section: When and how to pay the SEVIS fee
text: The student needs the Form I-20 before paying. A student outside the United States who needs a visa must pay before the visa interview and allow at least three business days for verification. The fee cannot be paid at the port of entry. Payment is made online by card at fmjfee.com, or by check or money order, or by Western Union Quick Pay. Cash and partial payments are not accepted. The student should keep the receipt, and its SEVIS ID must match the Form I-20.

title: Applying for a Schengen visa (European Commission)
text: A Schengen visa allows a national of a non-EU country to make a short visit of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. It can be single-entry, multiple-entry or for airport transit.

title: Applying for a Schengen visa (European Commission)
text: The applicant applies at the consulate of the country they plan to visit. If several Schengen countries are visited, the applicant applies at the consulate of the country where most time will be spent, or of the first country visited if the stays are equal. The application should be submitted at least 15 days before travel and no earlier than 6 months before. An appointment may be needed.

title: Applying for a Schengen visa (European Commission)
text: The applicant needs a passport that expires at least 3 months after leaving the Schengen area, a completed application form and an ICAO-compliant photo, and medical insurance covering emergency care, hospitalisation and repatriation. The applicant also provides documents on the purpose of the stay, financial means, accommodation and intention to return home. Fingerprints are collected at submission, with some exemptions. Consulates may ask for additional documents.

title: Applying for a Schengen visa (European Commission)
text: The Schengen visa fee is 90 euros for adults and 45 euros for children aged 6 to 12. Visa service centres may charge an extra fee, and some categories of applicants are exempt. A normal decision takes 15 days and can extend to 45 days if more examination or documents are needed.

title: Schengen area (European Commission)
text: The Schengen area has 29 countries: 25 EU Member States and 4 non-EU countries, which are Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Bulgaria and Romania joined on 1 January 2025. Cyprus takes part in Schengen cooperation but internal border controls have not yet been abolished. Ireland is not bound by the Schengen rules.

title: Student (France-Visas)
text: To apply for a French student long-stay visa, the applicant must be over 18, have chosen a course and have been accepted by a higher education establishment. The applicant checks whether their country follows the Etudes en France (EEF) procedure and, if not, the enrolment conditions on Campus France. Some first-year applicants must also use Parcoursup. A stay of more than 3 months needs a long-stay visa with a residence permit, which requires formalities after arrival in France.

title: Student (France-Visas)
text: The indicative visa fee is about 50 euros for countries on the Etudes en France procedure and about 99 euros for others. The applicant prepares the file with the France-Visas visa wizard and applies online, uploading legible digital copies of the documents. The essential document is a certificate of enrolment from the accepting higher education institution, together with proof of a temporary address for the first three months or the permanent address if already housed. After arrival, students under 28 from outside the EEA must also register for social security, which is free and mandatory.

title: Long Term Visa used as Residence Permit or VLS-TS (Campus France)
text: The VLS-TS student visa allows study in France for four months to one year, after which a residence permit is needed. The student applies at the prefecture for a multi-annual residence permit about three months before the visa expires, and its length matches the years remaining in the programme.

title: Long Term Visa used as Residence Permit or VLS-TS (Campus France)
text: The VLS-TS must be validated online, in a fully digital process, within 3 months of arrival in France. The student needs a valid email address, the visa information, the arrival date, the home address in France, and a bank card to pay the residence permit fee, or an electronic stamp bought with cash. Holders of a multiple-entry visa can travel freely in the first 3 months, but after that an unvalidated visa requires a new visa to re-enter France.

title: Long Term Visa used as Residence Permit or VLS-TS (Campus France)
text: A VLS-TS holder can travel freely within the Schengen area, work up to 964 hours per year, which is about 20 hours per week, and use the VISALE free rental guarantee. Students from the 73 countries under the Etudes en France procedure apply through that platform, and others contact their nearest French consulate.
